hints: Focus on the shapes before and after, since bond angle is decided by the number of bonding pairs and lone pairs around each central atom.
Start with boron: $\text{BF}_3$ is trigonal planar with $120^{\circ}$ angles, but in $\text{F}_3\text{B-NH}_3$ boron has four bonding pairs.

Now look at nitrogen: it loses the squeezing effect of its lone pair when that pair becomes the $\text{B-N}$ dative bond, so think about what happens to a pyramidal $107^{\circ}$ angle when it becomes tetrahedral.
walkthrough:
**Look at boron in BF3**

Think of $\text{BF}_3$ on its own. Boron has 3 bonding pairs and no lone pairs.

That gives a trigonal planar shape:
$$\text{F-B-F angle} = 120^{\circ}$$

**Look at boron in the product**

In $\text{F}_3\text{B-NH}_3$, boron accepts the lone pair from nitrogen to form a fourth bond. Now boron has 4 bonding pairs and no lone pairs.

That gives a tetrahedral arrangement around B:
$$\text{F-B-F angle} \approx 109.5^{\circ}$$
So the F-B-F angle decreases from $120^{\circ}$ to $109.5^{\circ}$.

**Look at nitrogen in NH3**

In $\text{NH}_3$, nitrogen has 3 bonding pairs plus 1 lone pair. The lone pair repels strongly and squeezes the bonds together.

That gives a trigonal pyramidal shape:
$$\text{H-N-H angle} \approx 107^{\circ}$$

**Look at nitrogen in the product**

When the lone pair is used to make the $\text{B-N}$ dative covalent bond, nitrogen now has 4 bonding pairs and no lone pairs.

That gives a tetrahedral arrangement around N:
$$\text{H-N-H angle} \approx 109.5^{\circ}$$
So the H-N-H angle increases from $107^{\circ}$ to $109.5^{\circ}$. Decreases then increases matches one row.

options.A: Half right and half wrong. F-B-F does decrease from $120^{\circ}$ to $109.5^{\circ}$, but H-N-H does not decrease. The lone pair on nitrogen is removed to form the dative bond, so repulsion is reduced and the angle opens up.
options.B: Correct and lovely VSEPR logic. Boron goes from 3 pairs (trigonal planar, $120^{\circ}$) to 4 pairs (tetrahedral, $109.5^{\circ}$) so angle decreases. Nitrogen goes from 3 bonds + 1 lone pair (pyramidal, $107^{\circ}$) to 4 bonds (tetrahedral, $109.5^{\circ}$) so angle increases.
options.C: Reversed thinking. Students choosing this often think adding a bond always increases angles. In fact boron gains electron pairs around it, so crowding increases and the $120^{\circ}$ planar angle must close down to tetrahedral.
options.D: The nitrogen part is correct (increases), but the boron part is not. $\text{BF}_3$ starts wide and flat at $120^{\circ}$. It cannot open up further when a fourth group joins, it must fold into a tetrahedron near $109.5^{\circ}$.
